# Replication comparison — Haushofer & Shapiro (QJE 2016)

*Generated by `Program/statspai/build_comparison.py`; do not edit by hand.*

Three columns are compared for every published cell:

| Source | What it is |
|---|---|
| **paper** | The authors' shipped LaTeX tables (`Materials/package_outputs/Tables`, April 2017). They are verified below, token by token, against the paper PDF shipped in the package (`Materials/Paper/Haushofer_Shapiro_UCT.pdf`), which is the **erratum-corrected** version (22 April 2017). |
| **Stata re-run** | `Program/run_original.do` → author's `MASTER.do` in Stata 18 MP, output in `Results/Tables` |
| **StatsPAI** | `Program/statspai/*.py` (statspai 1.28.0, Python 3.13), output in `Results/statspai` |

Flags: ✅ equal at the reported precision (2 decimals; N and USD integers exactly); ⚠️ differs only in a Monte-Carlo
cell (FWER permutation p-values, bootstrap SEs of Lee bounds, sqreg bootstrap SEs) or by one unit in the last digit
where the underlying estimate sits on a rounding knife-edge; ❌ real mismatch (none); – not produced by that route.

## Which version do the numbers match — published QJE (2016) or the 2017 erratum?

**Both the Stata re-run and StatsPAI reproduce the corrected (erratum) tables.**

* Erratum item 1 (FWER p-values used 1,000 instead of 10,000 permutations): MASTER.do sets
  `stepdowniternow = 10000`. Published-vs-corrected pairs such as Table II revenue [0.02]→[0.03] or
  female-recipient assets [0.52]→[0.51] move by ≤0.01, i.e. inside the Monte-Carlo band; our 10,000-draw
  re-runs land at [0.03] (Stata) / [0.02] (StatsPAI port) and [0.51] / [0.49] — consistent with either version,
  and the variation across seeds is of the same size as the erratum's changes.
* Erratum item 2 (Table III psychological index wrongly weighted): the code now runs unweighted and gives
  0.03 (0.07) in cols 1–4, the corrected values. Re-running the weighted specification
  (`[aw=weight2]`, `Results/statspai/table3_psych_preerratum_weighted.csv`) gives **0.11 (0.07), 0.10 (0.07),
  0.11 (0.07), 0.10 (0.07)** — exactly the originally published row, confirming the erratum's diagnosis.
* Erratum item 3 (Lee bounds omitted observations with missing outcomes): the corrected code pads the sample with the
  5 (10 for psych) "attriting" metal-roof upgraders; our Lee point estimates equal the corrected values in every cell.
  Lee bound SEs are bootstrapped (100 reps, unseeded in the author's code) and differ from both published versions by
  Monte-Carlo noise, as the erratum itself notes ("text printed in blue").

## Why StatsPAI needed hand-written pieces

* joint "SUR" tests (`suest … , cluster()` + `test`) — not available in StatsPAI (`sp.sureg` is FGLS SUR without
  cluster-robust cross-equation VCV); implemented from OLS influence functions (`uct_common.suest_wald`).
* FWER p-values — the authors' `stepdown.ado` is a placebo-treatment permutation stepdown; StatsPAI only has
  bootstrap Romano–Wolf (`sp.romano_wolf`), so the ado was ported (`uct_common.stepdown_perm`) and `sp.romano_wolf`,
  `sp.bonferroni/holm/benjamini_hochberg` are reported alongside (`Results/statspai/table2_multiple_testing.md`).
* Lee bounds — `sp.lee_bounds` uses a different trimming/tie convention; an exact port of `leebounds.ado`
  (including a Stata macro-precision quirk that decides whether the threshold observation is trimmed) reproduces the
  published bounds and analytic SEs exactly.
